title: The Autopsy of Saint Alder's
premise: When Saint Alder's founder Edmund Voss is exhumed for a bicentennial ceremony, Hazel Kavanagh opens the coffin to find it empty—except for a brass ledger key and a note in her predecessor's handwriting. Following a coded ledger hidden in the town archive, Hazel uncovers a century of staged deaths, swapped bodies, and a coastal smuggling network sustained by the town's most respected families, including her late mentor. As the tide threatens to expose the final resting place of the real Edmund Voss—and the child he fathered with a woman the town erased—Hazel must choose between protecting the found family that raised them and telling a truth that will bury Saint Alder's reputation. In the end, Hazel refiles the town's secrets not in the archive but in the open, reading the ledger aloud at the bicentennial, and finally belongs to a town that knows them completely.
about_author: Quentin Winterbourne is the pen name of a former maritime archivist who spent a decade cataloguing coastal town records before turning to fiction. They write mysteries about the weight of paper, the patience of water, and the towns that keep both.

chapters.title: Every Grave by Name
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Establishes Hazel's meticulous, invisible life as Saint Alder's coroner, their rituals of filing and their quiet devotion to the town. Opening the bicentennial preparations, Hazel feels the first tremor of change. Emotional beat: contentment laced with loneliness.

chapters.title: The Order of Exhumation
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. A court order arrives: founder Edmund Voss must be exhumed for DNA verification ahead of the bicentennial statue unveiling. Hazel's mentor, the late Corner Whitlock, signed the original burial record—oddly, in fresh-looking ink. Emotional beat: unease beneath professional calm.

chapters.title: Two Hundred Years of Dirt
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. The exhumation draws the whole town to the cemetery. Hazel notes who watches too closely: councilwoman Maren Voss-Teague, the founder's descendant, and Father Ibarra, who objects on strange procedural grounds. Emotional beat: the town as audience, Hazel as specimen.

chapters.title: Empty
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. The coffin holds no body—only a brass ledger key and a note in Whitlock's handwriting: 'Hazel, you already know where it starts.' Hazel hides both before anyone else sees. Emotional beat: vertigo; the ground of Hazel's life gives way.

chapters.title: Filing Error
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Hazel searches Whitlock's old files and finds the burial record altered, the death certificate referencing a ledger volume that doesn't exist in the archive index. Deputy Sam Okafor, Hazel's only friend, notices Hazel's distraction. Emotional beat: first crack in loyalty.

chapters.title: What Maren Wants
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. Councilwoman Voss-Teague pressures Hazel to declare the exhumation a clerical error and reseal the grave before the ceremony. Her charm has teeth. Hazel realizes the Voss family expected the empty coffin—or feared it. Emotional beat: menace in politeness.

chapters.title: The Ledger That Isn't There
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Following the key's engraving—a shelf number—Hazel finds a hollowed archive volume: a coded ledger of initials, dates, and payments spanning a century. The last entry is dated three weeks before Whitlock's death. Emotional beat: dread of inheritance.

chapters.title: Sam Asks Questions
chapters.summary: Sam's POV. Deputy Okafor pulls the file on Whitlock's death—ruled a heart attack on Hazel's own signature—and finds the responding officer's report missing. He confronts Hazel gently. Emotional beat: friendship strained by secrets kept 'to protect.'

chapters.title: The Tide Takes Inventory
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Ledger coordinates point to the drowned cove below Voss Cliff. At low tide Hazel finds a collapsed sea cave entrance and a rusted chain. The tide timetable becomes a countdown. Emotional beat: the sea as accomplice and threat.

chapters.title: Father Ibarra's Confession, Partial
chapters.summary: Ibarra's POV. The priest admits Whitlock came to him before dying, seeking absolution for 'a kindness that was a theft.' He won't say more, bound by the confessional, but slips Hazel a funeral card with a date circled: 1954. Emotional beat: guilt as architecture.

chapters.title: The 1954 Drowning
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Newspaper archives reveal a 1954 drowning: a Voss child, officially lost at sea, whose body was 'recovered' by then-coroner Ambrose Pell—the same man whose records Whitlock altered. Emotional beat: the past pressing its hand flat on the present.

chapters.title: Someone Searched My Office
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Hazel returns to find the office ransacked, the hidden volume's decoy taken. A threatening note in elegant script: 'Some filings are permanent.' Hazel realizes they are being managed, not warned. Emotional beat: fear sharpening into defiance.

chapters.title: The Historical Society's Kind Women
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Three elderly society volunteers—the Braid sisters—reveal, obliquely, that 'everyone knows the Voss men are buried twice.' They've kept the town's oral ledger for generations. One slips Hazel a photograph of Whitlock with an unknown woman. Emotional beat: found family offering its first thread.

chapters.title: The Woman in the Photograph
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. The woman is Lark Odell, a housekeeper at Voss Hall who vanished in 1954 with the drowned child's death record. Census traces place her son—born that spring—in the next county, adopted. Emotional beat: Hazel's obsession turning personal.

chapters.title: Resealing the Grave
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. Maren forces through an emergency council vote to reseal and declare the exhumation void. She privately burns a letter from her grandfather instructing 'the arrangement' be maintained. Her loyalty to the family name is absolute and corrosive. Emotional beat: villainy with a loving heart.

chapters.title: Sam Chooses a Side
chapters.summary: Sam's POV. Sam discovers the missing officer report was signed by the current sheriff, Delacroix—a Voss cousin by marriage. He tells Hazel he's in, whatever it costs. Emotional beat: loyalty chosen, not inherited.

chapters.title: The Code in Plain Sight
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Hazel cracks the cipher: entries are keyed to hymn numbers in the church's 1911 hymnal, which Ibarra still uses. Decoded, the ledger tracks payments for 'maintenance of arrangement'—coffin swaps protecting smugglers, then something darker: protecting a living Voss. Emotional beat: the thrill of the lock opening.

chapters.title: Whitlock's Last Filing
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. In Whitlock's lakeside cabin, Hazel finds his true confession, unfinished: he discovered the founder's coffin empty decades ago and was co-opted into the cover-up, spending his life leaving a trail only Hazel could follow. The last line: 'The real one is where the tide keeps him.' Emotional beat: grief for a mentor who was also a keeper of lies.

chapters.title: The Sheriff's Courtesy Call
chapters.summary: Delacroix's POV. The sheriff visits Hazel with friendly warnings about 'town stability,' revealing he knows about the cabin visit. He offers Hazel Whitlock's old job and silence. Hazel declines. Emotional beat: the machinery of respectability showing its gears.

chapters.title: Voss Hall at Night
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Hazel breaks into the decaying Voss Hall and finds Edmund Voss's private study preserved like a shrine—and a second ledger, the family's own, matching the coded one entry for entry, plus letters between Edmund and Lark Odell. Emotional beat: intimacy with the dead founder.

chapters.title: The Letters of Edmund and Lark
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. The letters reveal Edmund faked his own death in 1824 to escape debts, letting the town deify a ghost while he lived hidden, fathering a child with Lark. The 'arrangement' protected the myth—and the fortune Maren inherited. Emotional beat: the founder as fraud; faith as inventory.

chapters.title: What the Bicentennial Is Really For
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. Maren learns Hazel has the letters and realizes the statue unveiling must proceed at any cost—the Voss fortune's legal basis rests on the founder's death record. She authorizes Delacroix to act. Emotional beat: a woman choosing the lie that raised her.

chapters.title: The Braid Sisters' Warning
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. The Braid sisters tell Hazel the last person who asked about Lark Odell—a journalist in 1987—drowned in the cove, ruled accidental by Whitlock. Hazel understands Whitlock's guilt and the pattern: the town drowns its questions. Emotional beat: terror wearing the face of history.

chapters.title: Sam Is Suspended
chapters.summary: Sam's POV. Delacroix suspends Sam on fabricated charges, isolating Hazel from official protection. Sam, undeterred, starts pulling records from the county seat. Emotional beat: the cost of belonging to the truth instead of the town.

chapters.title: The Child Who Lived
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Hazel locates Lark's descendants: a great-granddaughter, Ruth, living quietly nearby, who possesses Lark's diary. The diary confirms the child—Edmund's line—was smuggled out the night of the staged drowning, and that Whitlock helped years later. Emotional beat: a living thread through the lie.

chapters.title: DNA and Leverage
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Ruth's DNA could prove the founder's line lives—and that Maren's inheritance rests on a false death. But going public exposes Ruth's family to the town that erased Lark. Ruth hesitates; Hazel refuses to decide for her. Emotional beat: truth as something that must be consented to.

chapters.title: The Tide Table
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Whitlock's note and the ledger's final coordinates converge: the founder's actual remains—and evidence of the 1987 journalist—lie in the sea cave, exposed only by an extreme low tide in nine days, the morning after the unveiling. Emotional beat: a deadline set by the moon.

chapters.title: Delacroix Makes It Official
chapters.summary: Delacroix's POV. Ordered to 'handle' Hazel, Delacroix stages a break-in at Hazel's home and files charges of evidence tampering. Hazel's license is suspended; their invisibility weaponized against them. Emotional beat: exile inside one's own town.

chapters.title: The Town Picks Sides
chapters.summary: Multiple brief POVs. The Braid sisters, Ibarra, and half the town quietly rally—leaving food, alibis, photocopied records on Hazel's porch. Saint Alder's reveals it was never as asleep as it seemed. Emotional beat: found family materializing out of ordinary neighbors.

chapters.title: Maren Reads the Letters
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. Hazel sends Maren the Edmund–Lark letters anonymously. Maren confronts the truth that her revered ancestor lived a lie and her fortune is theft from a living line. She wavers—then doubles down, scheduling the unveiling for the night before the extreme tide. Emotional beat: grief curdling into desperation.

chapters.title: The Cave at Half Tide
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Hazel and Sam scout the cave early and find recent tool marks—someone has been maintaining it. They recover a sealed lead box: the journalist's notes and a bone fragment. They must leave it; the full reveal needs the low tide. Emotional beat: evidence within reach, hands forced empty.

chapters.title: Whitlock's Second Note
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Inside the lead box's wrapping, a second note from Whitlock: he didn't kill the journalist—he staged the drowning and hid the man alive in exile, the town's one mercy. The journalist, now old, is alive in the next county. Emotional beat: Whitlock redeemed just enough to break Hazel's heart.

chapters.title: The Witness in Exile
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Hazel and Sam find the aged journalist, Elias Marsh, who has waited thirty-seven years for someone to come asking. He gives his testimony and photographs. Emotional beat: patience vindicated; a debt finally collected.

chapters.title: The Night Before
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. On unveiling eve, Hazel assembles everything—ledger, letters, diary, DNA kit, testimony—into a single 'file' and realizes the only archive that can't be burned or buried is the town itself, gathered in one place. Maren's people watch Hazel's house. Emotional beat: terrible calm before the choice.

chapters.title: The Unveiling
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. The statue is unveiled to applause; Maren gives a speech about legacy. Hazel walks to the front and asks for the town's attention. Delacroix moves to intervene—but half the council, seeded by the Braid sisters, stands with Hazel. Emotional beat: the moment the town holds its breath.

chapters.title: Reading the Ledger Aloud
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Hazel reads the decoded ledger, the letters, and Lark's diary to the assembled town as the tide begins its historic retreat. Shock, denial, weeping. Maren demands Hazel's arrest; the crowd does not move. Emotional beat: truth as a public act, not a private filing.

chapters.title: What the Tide Gave Back
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. At dawn, the extreme low tide opens the cave. Before the town, state investigators, and Ruth Odell's family, the remains of Edmund Voss and the journalist's evidence are recovered. Maren, seeing Ruth's face—her family's living mirror—finally breaks and confesses her part. Emotional beat: the sea settling its account.

chapters.title: Reburial
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Edmund Voss is buried again—this time truly, without myth, his headstone amended to name Lark Odell beside him. Ibarra offers a service that is more honesty than eulogy. Hazel's suspension is lifted; Delacroix resigns. Emotional beat: mourning without the lie.

chapters.title: The New Filing System
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Hazel reopens the archive with a new principle: nothing sealed without a reason, nothing hidden without a date. Sam is elected sheriff; Ruth donates Lark's diary to the public record. The Braid sisters appoint themselves overseers. Emotional beat: repair as ongoing work.

chapters.title: Belonging, Alphabetized
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Months later, Hazel walks the cemetery at dusk, knowing every grave by name—and being known by name in return. A child asks Hazel about the empty coffin, and Hazel tells the truth, simply. The tide comes in, patient and clean. Emotional beat: invisibility traded, gladly, for belonging.
